# Distributed training

**Read:** [CS336 L7](https://github.com/stanford-cs336/spring2025-lectures/blob/4eff81bee0a853217209e163936b264f03572b66/nonexecutable/2025%20Lecture%207%20-%20Parallelism%20basics.pdf)–[8](http://cs336.stanford.edu/spring2025-lectures/?trace=var/traces/lecture_08.json); [Scaling book ch. 3](https://jax-ml.github.io/scaling-book/sharding), [ch. 5](https://jax-ml.github.io/scaling-book/training), [ch. 12 (GPUs)](https://jax-ml.github.io/scaling-book/gpus); [ZeRO](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.02054); [Megatron-LM](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.08053); [CS336 A2](https://github.com/stanford-cs336/assignment2-systems)

**Must master:** Data parallel (AllReduce gradients) vs tensor parallel (split weight matrices, AllGather activations) vs pipeline parallel (micro-batches to shrink the bubble) vs expert parallel; ZeRO stages 1–3; rematerialization, gradient accumulation, host offload; roofline reasoning (compute vs memory vs communication bound); "5D parallelism"

**HAND implementation:** A memory-math worksheet: params, grads, Adam states, activations per GPU under each scheme (HAND, on paper); the distributed trainer itself is AGENT, from CS336 A2

**Known interview question:** "8 × 80 GB A100s, 70B model — walk me through memory math and parallelism strategy." "What is 5D parallelism?"
